extraFacts.fact: Pressure conversion used in these answers: 1 bar = 14.5038 psi, so 100 psi is about 7 bar, 125 psi about 9 bar, 145 psi about 10 bar, 150 psi about 10 bar, 160 psi about 11 bar, 175 psi about 12 bar, 200 psi about 14 bar, 215 psi about 15 bar, 220 psi about 15 bar, 250 psi about 17 bar, 290 psi about 20 bar, 300 psi about 21 bar and 500 psi about 34 bar.
extraFacts.source: ISO 80000-4 / NIST SP 811 unit conversion (1 bar = 100 kPa = 14.5038 psi)

extraFacts.fact: FRL line order and roles: in a compressed-air line the usual order is filter, then regulator, then lubricator, with the lubricator last before the tool or cylinder. The filter protects the regulator and tools from dirt and water, the regulator sets a steady working pressure, and the lubricator adds oil mist only while air is flowing. Size units on port size and on the air flow the downstream tools need, not on line size alone.
extraFacts.source: Indus guide /blog/frl-filter-regulator-lubricator-guide; maker FRL catalogues (Parker 0700P, Norgren, SMC)

extraFacts.fact: Filter grades: a particulate filter removes solids and bulk liquid water down to its micron grade; a coalescing filter removes oil aerosol and very fine particles and needs a particulate pre-filter upstream; an activated-carbon filter removes oil vapour and odour and is placed after a coalescing filter. ISO 8573-1 is the standard that sets compressed-air purity classes for solid particles, water and oil, and a single filter stage does not by itself guarantee a class.
extraFacts.source: ISO 8573-1 (compressed air purity classes); Indus guide /blog/compressed-air-quality-iso-8573-1; maker catalogues

extraFacts.fact: Bowls: polycarbonate bowls can be attacked by some synthetic compressor oils, solvents and cleaning chemicals, and should be cleaned with mild soap and water only; metal bowls with a sight glass are used where those chemicals are present or where a plastic bowl is not permitted. Pressure and temperature ratings of plastic and metal bowl versions differ and are given per part number.
extraFacts.source: Maker catalogue bowl cautions (Parker 0700P Prep-Air II, Norgren, SMC)

extraFacts.fact: Regulators: a relieving regulator vents excess downstream pressure through the bonnet when the setting is turned down, while a non-relieving regulator holds the pressure until the load uses it. A regulator is set by turning the adjusting knob up to the working pressure on the gauge, and the inlet rating and the outlet adjustment range are separate figures. A regulator that creeps or will not hold its setting usually has dirt on the seat or a worn diaphragm.
extraFacts.source: Maker catalogues (Norgren, ARO, Parker); Indus guide /blog/frl-filter-regulator-lubricator-guide

extraFacts.fact: Lubricators: a mist (oil-fog) lubricator sends the drops it meters into the air stream and suits a single tool or cylinder close by; a micro-mist (micro-fog) lubricator returns the larger drops to the bowl and sends only fine particles, which travel further and can feed several points or a longer pipe run. Both feed oil only while air is flowing, and the lubricant should be the oil the maker recommends.
extraFacts.source: Maker catalogues (Parker 0700P, Norgren, Dixon); Indus guide /blog/frl-filter-regulator-lubricator-guide

extraFacts.fact: Harmonized System headings: 8421.39 covers filtering or purifying machinery and apparatus for gases (compressed-air filters); 8421.99 covers parts of such filters (replacement filter elements); 8481.10 covers pressure-reducing valves (air regulators); 8481.80 covers other taps, cocks and valves. Customs authorities classify combination units and lubricators individually, commonly under 8421.39, 8481.10 or 8481.80.
extraFacts.source: World Customs Organization, Harmonized System Nomenclature 2022, headings 84.21 and 84.81

extraFacts.fact: Flow ratings in cfm or scfm are quoted by the maker at a stated inlet pressure and pressure drop, so a unit sized on port size alone can drop pressure at full flow; check the flow curve or the row for the part you order.
